bio: This locale that used to house Le Spuller hotel and restaurant has been given a new lease of life and a Latin name that nods to the supposed etymological root of Sombernon. Behind an off-white façade with green shutters, the two spacious dining rooms are done out in a contemporary brasserie style. One has a counter, hardwood flooring, velvet banquettes and an Art Deco-style glass "ceiling"; the other, with views onto the countryside, is more intimate. Fresh and expressive dishes include gyoza with the last of the summer vegetables or pike-perch, spinach, mussels and "fish essence".
